string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and one of the world\'s most populous capital cities, with a history stretching back more than three thousand years. It served as the seat of the Ming and Qing dynasties, leaving iconic landmarks such as the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, and the Summer Palace. Surrounded by mountains to the north and west, Beijing is the country\'s political, cultural, and educational centre, housing the central government, leading universities, and major museums. It hosted the 2008 Summer Olympics and the 2022 Winter Olympics, making it the first city to stage both versions of the Games.

Shanghai is one of the four direct-administered municipalities of China and the country\'s largest and most influential global financial centre. Located on the southern shore of the Yangtze River estuary, it began as a small fishing town and grew rapidly after opening to foreign trade in the mid-nineteenth century. The famous Bund waterfront displays European-style buildings, while the Lujiazui skyline across the Huangpu River features the Oriental Pearl Tower and some of the world\'s tallest skyscrapers. With a major container port, busy airports, and a population of over twenty-four million, Shanghai drives much of China\'s international commerce.

Chongqing is a large direct-administered municipality in southwestern China, located at the meeting point of the Yangtze River and the Jialing River. Unlike flat coastal cities, it is built across steep hills and river valleys, which earned it the nickname Mountain City. It became a direct-administered municipality in 1997 and serves as a major industrial and transport hub, with dense high-rise districts, dramatic riverside bridges, and the busy Chaotianmen wharf. Chongqing is also the starting point of many Yangtze River cruises, and it is famous for its spicy hotpot cuisine, winter fog, and the ancient Buddhist rock carvings at Dazu.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality and major port city in northern China, sitting on the coast of the Bohai Sea about one hundred kilometres southeast of Beijing. It was opened as a treaty port in the nineteenth century, and its colonial past is still visible in the historic villas and European-style buildings of the Five Great Avenues. The city blends this heritage with modern landmarks such as the Tianjin Eye, a giant Ferris wheel built over the Hai River, and the gleaming skyscrapers of its central business district. As northern China\'s key shipping and manufacturing centre, Tianjin connects the capital region to global sea trade routes.
